primary_sources.source: ISO/IEC 25010:2023, Systems and software Quality Requirements and Evaluation (SQuaRE) — Product quality model
primary_sources.type: International voluntary standard; official ISO catalogue and abstract
primary_sources.relevance: Defines a nine-characteristic product-quality reference model for ICT and software products and supports requirements, test objectives, quality-control criteria, acceptance criteria, and measures. It is appropriate for organizing prototype quality evaluation, but the public abstract does not supply clause-level measures or authorize an undifferentiated claim that the prototype is ISO compliant.

primary_sources.source: ISO/IEC 25012:2008, Software engineering — SQuaRE — Data quality model
primary_sources.type: International voluntary standard; official ISO catalogue and browsable definitions
primary_sources.relevance: Defines a general model for structured data, with fifteen characteristics viewed as inherent or system-dependent, for establishing requirements, measures, and evaluations in production, acquisition, and integration. ISO defines data quality as the degree to which data characteristics satisfy stated and implied needs under specified conditions. This supports context-specific measurement of accuracy, completeness, consistency, credibility, currentness, traceability, accessibility, availability, confidentiality, efficiency, precision, compliance, understandability, portability, and recoverability.

primary_sources.source: Brooke, J. (1996), SUS: A quick and dirty usability scale
primary_sources.relevance: Introduces the ten-item System Usability Scale as a low-cost global subjective assessment scored as a single 0–100 value. Brooke explicitly treats usability as context-dependent. SUS therefore complements, but does not replace, observed task completion, error, accessibility, information-quality, or operational-effectiveness measures.

Provides technology-independent, testable success criteria and conformance requirements for full pages. It supports systematic keyboard, focus, labels, contrast, status-message, reflow, target-size, error-identification, and assistive-technology checks. Automated scans alone cannot establish conformance, and following WCAG does not address every disability-related need.

primary_sources.source: Hristidis et al. (2007), Data Quality for Situational Awareness during Mass-Casualty Events
primary_sources.relevance: Compares a wireless disaster information system with paper-based tracking and reports lower information latency and richer information while documenting that component failures can delay delivery and degrade display usefulness. It supports testing timeliness, completeness, failure visibility, and degraded-network behavior rather than assuming digitization is uniformly beneficial.

primary_sources.source: Norri-Sederholm et al. (2015), Shared situational awareness and information quality in disaster management
primary_sources.relevance: Develops a framework connecting critical information requirements and information quality gaps in disaster management and emphasizes timely, accurate, relevant information for actors. It supports role- and task-specific quality criteria; it does not prove that any particular dashboard creates shared situational awareness.

Distinguishes formative, process, outcome, and impact evaluation; requires credible evidence, explicit limitations, and a design suited to the evaluation question. It states that outcome evaluation does not itself attribute causality, whereas impact evaluation compares outcomes with and without the intervention. This is directly relevant to baseline workflow comparisons and restrained effect claims.

evidence.legal_or_evidentiary_status: ISO/IEC 25010:2023 and ISO/IEC 25012:2008 are recognized voluntary standards, not Philippine statutory duties unless adopted through law, regulation, procurement, contract, or institutional policy. Their models can structure requirements and evaluation, but using selected characteristics is not evidence of certification or conformity. WCAG 2.2 is a W3C Recommendation with normative success criteria; a conformance claim requires all applicable criteria at the claimed level across full pages and accessibility-supported technologies. Brooke's SUS is an original standardized subjective usability instrument, not an effectiveness, safety, accessibility, or data-quality certification. The disaster-information articles are empirical or analytical academic evidence whose findings are bounded by their systems, exercises, participants, and response contexts. The CDC framework is official evaluation guidance and supports the logic of comparison and attribution limits, but does not prescribe thresholds for this prototype.
evidence.evidence_limits_and_conflicts: The complete normative texts of ISO/IEC 25010:2023 and ISO/IEC 25012:2008 are copyrighted and were not fully available through their official public catalogue pages; the study may cite their official scope and definitions but should verify purchased or library-accessed text before reproducing characteristics, clauses, or claiming exact conformance. The WIISARD study concerns mass-casualty medical response and older wireless technology; its direction of effect cannot be transferred as an expected effect size for Philippine LGU reporting. Shared-situational-awareness research establishes the importance of fit-for-purpose information quality, not a causal guarantee from aggregation. SUS produces perceived-usability scores that can remain high despite task errors or inaccessible flows. A before/after or same-participant prototype comparison is vulnerable to practice, order, novelty, instrumentation, and selection effects. Accuracy cannot be measured without a defensible reference set, and expert labels may disagree. Currentness is not merely the newest timestamp: late but valid observations, corrections, and different as-of times must be retained. Duplicate detection and conflict detection are different tasks; two reports about one event may provide independent corroboration rather than duplication. No source supports claims that this student evaluation proves casualty reduction, faster official response, nationwide effectiveness, regulatory compliance, product-market fit, or causal impact.

chapter_one_integration.objective_revisions: Add an evaluation objective tied to the existing submodules: evaluate User and Organization Management through task success, least-privilege enforcement, and cross-organization isolation; Disaster Reporting through applicable-field completeness, time/source capture, duplicate handling, and reporting-task time; Verification through provenance coverage, conflict-detection precision and recall, correct status assignment, and retained decisions; SitRep Generation through aggregation accuracy, snapshot reproducibility, source traceability, correction/supersession fidelity, and generation time; Catalog through code validity, version consistency, and prevention of incompatible-unit aggregation; and Dashboard through interpretation accuracy, freshness/uncertainty comprehension, task completion, accessibility checks, and perceived usability. Compare representative prototype tasks with the current document or spreadsheet workflow using the same scenario data and explicitly reported conditions. The objective should say 'assess' or 'compare,' not 'prove effectiveness.'
chapter_one_integration.scope_inclusions: Include representative authorized roles, the six named submodules, task scenarios derived from actual reporting work, a deliberately seeded reference dataset, and a documented baseline workflow. The dataset should contain complete and incomplete reports, unknown values, late submissions, exact and near duplicates, contradictory values, corrections, differing geographic scopes, mixed units, provisional and verified claims, and source documents. Evaluation records should include participant role and relevant experience, training, device/browser, assistive technology where applicable, network condition, task order, start/end times, task outcome, critical and noncritical errors, assistance, SUS responses, open comments, and evaluator observations. Include product-quality tests selected from ISO/IEC 25010:2023, data-quality measures selected from ISO/IEC 25012:2008, WCAG 2.2 checks, role/tenant security tests, and restore/export checks only where implemented. Preserve raw observations and calculation rules so reported results are reproducible.
chapter_one_integration.limitations_and_delimitations: The evaluation is a prototype assessment, not an ISO certification, WCAG audit by an accredited body, penetration test, clinical/public-safety trial, operational deployment, economic evaluation, or market-validation study. It should not test unimplemented dispatch, forecasting, sensor integration, official warning issuance, nationwide interoperability, or fully offline operation. A small purposive sample can identify severe usability problems and estimate performance in the tested tasks, but cannot represent every Philippine LGU, hazard, language, disability, device, or operational tempo. Prepared scenarios do not recreate stress, fatigue, damaged infrastructure, incomplete authority, or rapidly evolving ground truth. Treat SUS as descriptive for the tested sample and report the distribution and sample size. Do not calculate accuracy from fields for which the reference answer is legitimately ambiguous; record them as contested or exclude them by a stated rule.

significance_causal_chains.reporters: Structured, progressive capture plus visible required fields may increase applicable-field completeness and reduce avoidable omissions; the immediate outputs are completion ratios, error types, and task time. Operational benefit requires forms that match local terminology and do not delay urgent partial reports. Harm can arise from excessive mandatory fields or false precision.
significance_causal_chains.verifiers: Source-linked claims and explicit conflict queues may improve detection and resolution traceability; measure conflict precision/recall, provenance coverage, decision errors, and time. Benefit requires a reliable reference set and trained reviewers. False positives can waste attention, while false negatives can conceal contradictions.
significance_causal_chains.SitRep developers and approvers: A fixed cut-off snapshot with version lineage may improve aggregation correctness and reproducibility and reduce manual copying; measure correct cells over applicable cells, untraceable claims, and completion time against the baseline. Benefits depend on valid source data and compatible definitions; a polished but wrong aggregate is a plausible harm.
significance_causal_chains.decision makers: Freshness, verification state, denominators, and drill-down may improve interpretation of what is known, unknown, and contested; test scenario questions rather than infer comprehension from viewing time. Better interface interpretation does not establish better incident outcomes.
significance_causal_chains.customer organizations and startup: A transparent evaluation can identify readiness gaps, training needs, support burden, and deployment conditions. It can justify iterative product decisions, but not revenue, willingness to pay, or scalable adoption without customer and cost evidence.
significance_causal_chains.future researchers: Operational definitions, reference datasets, and raw results enable replication and refinement. Generalizable conclusions require larger, multisite, hazard-diverse, and preferably prospective studies.

safe: The prototype was evaluated under specified scenarios against the current workflow using the same reference data.

In the tested sample and tasks, the prototype produced a measured difference in median task time, applicable-field completeness, or aggregation accuracy; the exact result and uncertainty should be reported.
ISO/IEC 25010:2023 and ISO/IEC 25012:2008 informed the selection and definition of product- and data-quality measures.
SUS measured participants' perceived usability after completing the defined tasks and was interpreted alongside observed task performance.
Accessibility testing covered the listed WCAG 2.2 criteria, pages, browsers, and assistive technologies; findings are limited to that test scope.
The evaluation detected specific usability, provenance, consistency, accessibility, or workflow issues requiring revision.
avoid: The system is ISO certified, ISO compliant, or WCAG compliant based only on a student checklist.
A high SUS score proves that the system is effective, safe, accessible, or easy for all users.
The platform provides real-time, accurate, complete, or conflict-free information without operational definitions and measured results.
The prototype caused improved disaster response based on a post-test-only, before/after, or simulated comparison.
Duplicate removal always improves data quality; legitimate corroborating reports may share content.
The evaluation demonstrates nationwide suitability, casualty reduction, or startup viability.

authority_and_responsibility_matrix.research_lead: Defines questions, preregisters or freezes metrics and exclusions before analysis, controls study records, and reports adverse or unexpected findings and limitations.
authority_and_responsibility_matrix.domain_expert: Builds or reviews scenario truth sets, resolves genuinely ambiguous reference items by documented consensus, and does not silently change ground truth after seeing system output.
authority_and_responsibility_matrix.participant: Performs only tasks authorized for the assigned role, provides consent where required, and may withdraw without affecting employment or academic standing.
authority_and_responsibility_matrix.task_observer: Uses a fixed protocol to record time, assistance, errors, and task outcome without coaching except under a predefined rescue rule.
authority_and_responsibility_matrix.accessibility_evaluator: Combines automated checks with keyboard and assistive-technology inspection and states tested pages, criteria, tools, browsers, and unresolved issues.
authority_and_responsibility_matrix.customer_authority: Confirms that the baseline workflow, task scenarios, roles, terminology, and acceptable risks reflect actual organizational practice; retains operational authority.
authority_and_responsibility_matrix.startup_or_developer: Supplies the tested build and fixes defects but should not alter raw evaluation records or serve as the sole judge of success where conflicts of interest exist.
authority_and_responsibility_matrix.data_or_privacy_custodian: Approves de-identification, access, retention, secure storage, permitted reuse, and disposal of participant and operational records.

system_and_governance.workflow_lineage_and_data_lifecycle: Freeze and identify the prototype build, catalog version, baseline template, scenario dataset, reference-answer version, task script, devices, and network profile before each evaluation run. Assign pseudonymous participant and session IDs. Preserve source scenario records; expected duplicate groups, conflicts, applicable fields, and expected aggregates; timestamps; observer logs; screen or system logs where consented; computed metrics; exclusions; and analysis version. Corrections to the reference set must create a new version with reason and reviewer rather than overwrite prior labels. Maintain a calculation dictionary specifying numerators, denominators, missing-data treatment, unit normalization, time boundaries, and whether assistance counts as success. Separate research data from production/customer data, restrict access, and avoid collecting unnecessary personal or incident details. Publish only aggregated or de-identified results, document suppressed small cells, retain records under an approved schedule, and log deletion. This lineage lets another evaluator reproduce each table from the frozen raw data without treating the application's own output as ground truth.

module_specific_requirements.User and Organization Management: Script allowed and prohibited actions for reporter, verifier, approver, administrator, and viewer; test role changes, deactivated users, direct-object references, and cross-tenant reads and writes. Report prohibited attempts blocked over all prohibited attempts and every observed leakage, not only a percentage.
module_specific_requirements.Disaster Reporting: Calculate completeness only over fields applicable to that scenario and distinguish missing, unknown, not applicable, and zero. Measure correct source, occurred/observed/reported times, location, unit, attachment association, duplicate suggestions, false merges, error recovery, and task time.
module_specific_requirements.Verification: Use expert-labeled claims to compute provenance coverage, verification-state accuracy, conflict precision = true flagged conflicts/all flagged conflicts, conflict recall = true flagged conflicts/all reference conflicts, duplicate precision/recall, and retained rationale. Inspect false positives and false negatives because identical summary scores can hide different operational harms.
module_specific_requirements.SitRep Generation: Compare every applicable generated claim and aggregate with the versioned reference snapshot; test cut-off boundaries, late records, corrected values, incompatible scopes/units, verified-versus-provisional separation, source footnotes, report numbering, approvals, and supersession. Regenerate the same snapshot to test reproducibility.
module_specific_requirements.Catalog: Test valid-code selection, effective dates, aliases, unit compatibility, used-code immutability, version migration, and readable local labels. Seed obsolete and incompatible entries and confirm the system rejects or visibly handles them rather than silently recoding records.
module_specific_requirements.Dashboard: Give role-relevant questions requiring identification of total, denominator, as-of time, verification state, conflict, and source. Score answers, not impressions. Test keyboard-only completion, focus order and visibility, programmatic labels, chart alternatives, reflow/zoom, contrast, status messages, and screen-reader announcements on the pages actually evaluated.

system_and_governance.risk_controls_and_residual_limits: Use de-identified synthetic or approved historical scenarios, least-privilege access, encrypted storage and transport, consented recording, a predefined observer rescue protocol, and a stop rule if tests expose real sensitive data or tenant leakage. Counterbalance baseline/prototype order where feasible; otherwise disclose learning effects. Use the same scenario difficulty, task instructions, time rule, and assistance rule across conditions. Blind expert labeling to system output where feasible, use two reviewers for ambiguous conflicts, and record agreement and adjudication. Check calculation code against hand-worked cases and retain raw denominators. Accessibility requires human checks; automated tools find only a subset of failures. Residual limits include small-sample instability, Hawthorne and novelty effects, participant familiarity, artificial ground truth, evaluator/developer conflict of interest, inaccessible assistive-technology combinations not tested, and crisis conditions that cannot ethically or practically be simulated.

metrics_comparators_and_test_conditions.design: Use a within-participant counterbalanced comparison when feasible: each participant completes matched but nonidentical scenarios in the current workflow and prototype, with condition order alternated. If counterbalancing is infeasible, use separate comparable scenarios and disclose order effects. A post-test-only demonstration can find defects but cannot support an improvement claim.
primary_metrics: Task success = tasks completed to the predefined correct end state without critical error divided by attempted tasks; separately report assisted completion.
Applicable-field completeness = nonmissing applicable required fields divided by all applicable required fields; unknown and not-applicable are valid only when correctly used.
Field accuracy = reference-matching populated fields divided by populated fields eligible for comparison; report ambiguous/excluded fields separately.
Aggregation accuracy = correctly computed and scoped aggregate cells divided by all reference aggregate cells; also report absolute count and nature of errors.
Provenance coverage = displayed factual claims with retrievable source identifier and as-of/observation time divided by all displayed factual claims requiring provenance.
Currentness = age of each displayed claim at the report cut-off, plus proportion exceeding a stakeholder-defined freshness limit; never label the whole system real-time from server response speed.
Consistency violations = seeded or observed incompatible units, scopes, identifiers, or contradictory values left undisclosed divided by all tested consistency conditions.
Duplicate and conflict precision/recall, reported separately, using a versioned expert reference set.
Median and per-task completion time, critical/noncritical errors, requests for help, and recovery success; show raw distributions for small samples.
SUS total score calculated with Brooke's ten-item procedure after task exposure, with sample size and distribution; interpret as perceived usability only.
Accessibility results by WCAG 2.2 success criterion, page/state, severity, test method, browser, device, and assistive technology rather than one unsupported compliance percentage.
metrics_comparators_and_test_conditions.test_conditions: Report participant roles and experience; recruitment and exclusions; sample size; training; exact tasks and success criteria; build and dataset versions; baseline artifacts; desktop/mobile device, browser, resolution, input method and assistive technology; normal and degraded network profiles; permitted help; task timeout; order assignment; data-cleaning rules; and calculation formulas. Choose thresholds before viewing results and justify them using customer risk tolerance, existing workflow performance, or a stated acceptance need. Present counts with rates and denominators; for paired measurements report participant-level change or a suitable paired analysis, and avoid significance testing that a small convenience sample cannot support.
metrics_comparators_and_test_conditions.interpretation: A faster median with more critical errors is not improvement. A completeness gain produced by forced but fabricated entries is harm. A duplicate detector with high recall and poor precision may overload reviewers; a conflict detector with high precision and poor recall may conceal contradictions. Report trade-offs and failure cases. An outcome difference in a simulated comparison is evidence about those tasks and conditions, not causal evidence about real disaster outcomes.

evaluation_and_feasibility.adoption_cost_and_service_dependencies: Record evaluation and adoption inputs separately: participant and evaluator hours, training time, workflow mapping, catalog preparation, data cleansing/migration, accessibility remediation, security/privacy review, hosting, backup, monitoring, support, incident response, connectivity, devices, and integration maintenance. Compare task-time savings with new verification, administration, and support work rather than counting only faster document generation. Feasibility depends on customer staff who can maintain catalogs and reference sources, approve workflows, train users, and review conflicts; reliable identity, hosting, storage, export, and network services; accessible user support; and tested backup/restore and provider-exit procedures. A prototype evaluation may estimate observed labor per scenario but cannot establish total lifecycle cost, procurement readiness, willingness to pay, service-level performance, or scalable commercial demand without real deployments and financial/customer evidence.
evaluation_and_feasibility.generalization_and_future_evidence: Results cover only the tested build, participants, organization, roles, scenarios, hazards, language, devices, assistive technologies, dataset, and network conditions. Broader technical readiness needs larger datasets, load and concurrency tests, independent security/privacy review, recovery exercises, longitudinal defect and data-quality monitoring, and interface conformance tests. Broader usability and accessibility evidence needs participants across LGU levels, digital literacy, age, language, disability, device, and low-bandwidth conditions. Operational-effectiveness evidence needs prospective multisite exercises or deployments comparing a defensible baseline, tracking implementation fidelity, staffing, unintended effects, and sustained use. Causal public-safety claims require an impact design capable of estimating the counterfactual and controlling alternative explanations; routine outcome evaluation cannot supply this attribution. Economic claims need total-cost and benefit measurement; market claims need customer discovery, procurement evidence, retention, and willingness-to-pay data. Until then, conclusions should remain artifact- and context-specific and frame uncovered shortcomings as design requirements, not as proof of a universal solution.
